content_units: Cozy Friday Night Picks
A warm, funny, low-stress lineup that fits your filters: uplifting or witty tone, under 120 minutes, minimal gore, no heavy war themes, and comfortable for two adults plus a 13-year-old.
Option 1:   Paddington 2     Wholesome, clever, and consistently funny     103 min

- This is one of the safest crowd-pleasers around: sweet without being childish, witty without being cynical, and genuinely charming for adults too. Its humor is light and visual, and the story stays upbeat even when the characters hit obstacles.
- Content note: Very mild peril, a few tense chase/comedy moments, and no gore.
Watch trailer
Option 2:   The Princess Bride     Fairy-tale adventure with nonstop wit     98 min

- It blends romance, adventure, and comedy in a way that feels playful rather than intense, so it works well for a relaxed shared movie night. The dialogue is endlessly quotable, and the tone stays buoyant even during sword fights and escapes.
- Content note: Mild fantasy/action violence, brief scary moments, and no gore.
Watch trailer
Option 3:   School of Rock     Big-hearted comedy with great energy     109 min

- This is an easy win if you want something funny, upbeat, and fast-moving, with enough heart to keep it from feeling silly. It has strong family viewing appeal, but the jokes and performances also land well for adults.
- Content note: Mild rude humor, some rebellious school behavior, and no graphic content.
Watch trailer
Option 4:   Chef     Feel-good food movie with warmth and humor     114 min

- If you want a cozy movie in the literal sense, this is full of comfort-food energy, affectionate relationships, and an easygoing road-trip feel. It is uplifting and grown-up without being heavy, making it a nice middle ground for adults and a mature 13-year-old.
- Content note: Some strong language, brief sexual references, and no gore.
Watch trailer
Option 5:   Hunt for the Wilderpeople     Offbeat, funny, and unexpectedly tender     101 min

- This one has a quirky sense of humor and a lot of heart, with an adventurous setup that never turns dark or overwhelming. It balances laugh-out-loud moments with emotional warmth, so it feels cozy even while the characters are on the run.
- Content note: Mild action/peril, some coarse language, and no graphic violence.
Watch trailer
Best Match for Your Preferences
If you want the safest all-around pick, go with   Paddington 2  .
If you want the wittiest pick, choose   The Princess Bride  .
If you want the most cozy-for-adults option, pick   Chef  .
